title: Quantum Observation over Finite Holographic Substrate
content: We derive the measurement structure of quantum mechanics on a finite relational substrate that is the holographic encoding of observable space-time. The substrate is a finite field. Observer and observed system are cyclic subgroups of its multiplicative group, and observation is the quotient of the observed cycle by their shared core. The stationary states are the windings of the cycle, so E=hf is an identity. The measurement vectors are the transported characters of the core, a forced orthogonal basis whose completeness, selection rule and update are finite character theory. The squared amplitude counts phase-agreement pairs in the observer's tally ring, and on the stationary sector the count is uniform. The core two generic observers share is the quarter-turn group, whose tally ring is Z[i]; this is why amplitudes are complex. One drive conserves the relative offset of a pair, and the synchronised orbits are the Bell states. The Tsirelson bound saturates exactly S=2(ζ8+ζ8−1)=22, and with the analyser families inserted the construction reproduces the network table of complex quantum theory. The statistics beyond the stationary sector and the gravitational coupling enter as realisations, identifications of physical terms with substrate objects, each with its falsifier. Under the reciprocal-synchronisation realisation the same conservation makes gravity an entangling channel: equal force, unequal entanglement, with V2+C2=1 on the pure channel. Every exact statement has a machine check in finite-field or cyclotomic arithmetic and a proof in Lean, the counting theorems in an axiom-free core; the continuum enters only as a labelled degenerate idealisation. Each prediction names its falsifier.
